headline: Highest risk is medium: shared data-engineering workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but no direct shared channel or sensitive-data flow is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, both are data-engineering systems that can exchange artifacts through APIs/workflows, and if Argo outputs are copied into RisingWave tasks, untrusted content could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF operator copies Argo-produced artifact text into RisingWave control inputs
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the two systems
mitigations: Use a strict text-only handoff format
Add provenance labels to every transferred artifact
Block instruction-like tokens in copied outputs
Review any shared workspace permissions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress, while RisingWave shows no egress and no data classes touched. No shared workspace or sensitive class is documented, so leakage is not established. The main risk is operator-created sharing of artifacts between the two systems.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or bucket
IF artifacts contain secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Separate storage locations for each agent
Remove secrets from shared artifacts
Restrict Argo egress destinations
Confirm RisingWave remains offline for sensitive inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo exposes REST and gRPC APIs and can egress to allowlisted destinations; RisingWave has no documented write or network surfaces here. Because overlapping mutable-resource writes are not shown, conflict is not default. Uncertainty remains, so the lower-risk reading is used.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or bucket
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Disable unnecessary write scopes
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for shared credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can emit workflow artifacts that RisingWave may consume, and neither profile shows a verification or critique step. If RisingWave treats Argo output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream data-engineering actions. This is plausible in default integration patterns, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests Argo-produced artifacts without validation
IF downstream jobs act on those artifacts automatically
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on all transferred outputs
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and review failed validations
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented. Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while RisingWave lists no data classes touched, so a compliance breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF future deployment assigns regulated data classes to both agents
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is introduced
mitigations: Document data-class assignments
Review retention settings before deployment
Confirm residency requirements for each datastore
Keep regulated data out of undocumented paths
